summary: Wrote the missing unit tests for resolveRankedEligibility and the GeoHeaderSource contract of decidePaidDuelGeo (7 new tests, all invoking real exported functions, no source-text greps, no reimplemented logic). Ran a deliberate mutation (dropped the US-region allow-list check) and confirmed 5 tests across both rankedEligibility.test.ts and the pre-existing paidDuel.test.ts went red, then reverted and confirmed all green again — the gate is proven, not just claimed. Ran the full app (80 files / 745 tests) and orchestrator (15 suites / 58 tests) suites, app lint, app typecheck, orchestrator typecheck, and pack hygiene: all green. Independently reproduced the rendering-mode claim myself rather than trusting the handoff: built the working tree (ranked /duel and /duel/chips as f, dynamic) and, separately, built a detached git worktree at HEAD (ranked /duel and /duel/chips as o, static) — confirms the handoff's before/after claim byte-for-byte. Confirmed via grep that DuelHome and ChipDuelLobby have exactly one caller each (app/duel/page.tsx and app/duel/chips/page.tsx respectively) and no other caller was missed. Confirmed via diff that paidDuelGeo.ts's assertPaidDuelAllowed is a pure one-line delegate to the new decidePaidDuelGeo with zero logic change, and that all four real callers (guardPaidDuelRequest -> credits/checkout, plus direct calls from tournaments checkout/register and chips/match routes) are untouched by this diff. Confirmed the /api/geo/ranked JSON shape is unchanged (only a stale doc comment was corrected). Reverted the next-env.d.ts churn my own `pnpm build` run caused, per the prior handoff's flagged pitfall, and removed the temporary detached worktree and its symlinked node_modules. Did not commit or push; working tree carries only the software-engineer's original diff plus my new test file.
goal: Verify server-side paid-duel region eligibility (resolveRankedEligibility / decidePaidDuelGeo) on /duel and /duel/chips: true region decision on first paint, no optimistic 'available' default, no flash; shared edge-compatible headers-based helper; fail-closed posture and kill-switch gating intact. Add the unit tests the software-engineer explicitly left for the verifier.

openItemsForDownstream.message: The GeoHeaderSource.get() is documented as case-insensitive lookup in paidDuelGeo.ts's comment, but the underlying implementation (a real Headers object or next/headers()'s ReadonlyHeaders) provides that case-insensitivity, not decidePaidDuelGeo itself — decidePaidDuelGeo just calls .get(name) with the exact literal 'x-vercel-ip-country'. My test's headersFrom() helper reimplements case-insensitive lookup purely to mimic that real contract for the test double; it is not exercising a code path inside paidDuelGeo.ts. Worth a second look that no caller ever passes a header source that ISN'T case-insensitive.
openItemsForDownstream.action: Confirm both call sites (request.headers is a Fetch API Headers, and next/headers() headers() is Next's ReadonlyHeaders) really do normalize case, since decidePaidDuelGeo relies on that guarantee rather than doing its own toLowerCase().

openItemsForDownstream.message: No component-level test exists (and none existed before this change) for DuelHome or ChipDuelLobby rendering with initialGeoAllowed. The prop threading was verified by typecheck + full test suite + manual code read, not by a render test. This is a gap but matches pre-existing test coverage depth for these two components (neither had render tests before).
openItemsForDownstream.action: If a future change touches the geoBlocked/!geoAllowed branch again, a render test asserting the blocked-state UI actually appears for initialGeoAllowed=false would close this gap. Not blocking for this change since it's a pure prop-threading refactor with unchanged conditional logic (geoAllowed === false -> !geoAllowed is behaviorally identical once geoAllowed can never be null).

learnings.insight: A module-level const gated by an env var read at import time (PAID_DUELS_ENABLED) is testable in the same vitest process as call-time env reads (PAID_DUEL_GEO_ENFORCE) by combining vi.resetModules() + vi.stubEnv() + a dynamic `await import()` per test case, with vi.unstubAllEnvs() + vi.resetModules() in afterEach. No test helper or injectable parameter was needed, so the kill switch stayed genuinely un-bypassable while still being covered.
learnings.action: Reuse this pattern (resetModules + stubEnv + dynamic import) for any future module-level-const kill switch that must not gain an injectable bypass parameter.

learnings.insight: Feeding a deliberate mutation (removing the US-region allow-list branch) to the new AND pre-existing test files in the same run caught 5 failures across both files, confirming the new tests aren't redundant with the old ones — they cover the GeoHeaderSource/next-headers()-shaped input path specifically, which the Request-based paidDuel.test.ts never exercises.
learnings.action: When adding tests alongside an existing suite that covers overlapping logic through a different call path, run the mutation-proof against both files together, not just the new one — it demonstrates the new tests add real coverage rather than just re-asserting what was already proven.

learnings.insight: loop/learnings.md still carries an open question ('Subagent dispatch is disabled in this session — how should the duel geo fix proceed?') dated 2026-09-20 from earlier in this same run, but subagent dispatch (Agent tool with subagent_type=verifier) worked normally for this stage. That open question is now stale.
learnings.action: Remove the 'Subagent dispatch is disabled' open question from loop/learnings.md once the orchestrator confirms dispatch is working in the current session — leaving it in place will cause a future agent to needlessly re-litigate a resolved blocker.

learnings.insight: A detached `git worktree add <scratch> HEAD --detach` plus a symlinked node_modules (`ln -s <main-repo>/app/node_modules <worktree>/app/node_modules`) gives a from-scratch `next build` baseline in ~seconds instead of a full pnpm install, with zero risk to the working tree. Typing real DB credentials into a Bash command (even to `export` them) gets blocked by the permission classifier as credential materialization — rely on the profile-initialized shell environment instead (it's already present in every new Bash call in this environment) rather than re-exporting secret values yourself.
learnings.action: For any future before/after `next build` comparison, use a detached worktree with a symlinked node_modules, and never retype a DATABASE_URL/secret value into a command — let the shell's own profile-provided env vars carry it.
